notes: NO regulatory source. ESPR Art 9(2)(d) requires delegated acts to state whether a passport sits at model, batch or item level, but neither ESPR nor GS1 provides a family-level identifier. Supplying one is ADID's contribution, not a restatement of an existing standard.

Point (b) says the identifier is 'at the level indicated in the applicable delegated act'. Maps to ADID family/variant/instance. SYSTEM-ASSIGNED, not mapped from manufacturer input: ADID sets it from the level of the identifier it issues (family/variant/instance). Excluded from the mandatory input set for that reason.
A GTIN identifies one colour-and-size combination. It sits at variant level and can never represent a family (decisions.md D9).
Apparel-specific reading of point (f): care labelling is the garment sector's instructions-for-use.
Apparel-sector mandatory labelling. Required independently of ESPR; the textile delegated act is not yet adopted, so this is the firmest available basis for composition data.
Introduces BATCH granularity, which ESPR Art 9(2)(d) names (model/batch/item) but ADID's three levels do not carry. See the alignment note in cdm/ALIGNMENT.md — this is a real gap, not an oversight.
GTIN + serial = SGTIN = ADID instance level.

source_clause: DPP credentialSubject.productionDate; EPCIS eventTime at commissioning

notes: Distinct from countryOfOrigin, which is where the GARMENT was made. Fabric is routinely woven in one country and sewn in another — collapsing the two would misstate the supply chain.
A carbon figure without its declared unit is uninterpretable: 4.2 kg CO2e per garment and per kilogram are different claims.
UNTP's verification layer. Where ESPR Annex III 1(e) asks WHETHER compliance documentation exists, UNTP structures WHAT is claimed and who attests it.
Complements ESPR Annex III 1(i): the ESPR point mandates a facility IDENTIFIER, EPCIS supplies the location semantics around it.
